one_liner: Pure-Rust async Tokio CQL driver for ScyllaDB and Cassandra; the vendor's insert benchmark shows it level with the multi-threaded DataStax C++ driver.
what_it_does: A client library for the CQL binary protocol v4: build a Session with SessionBuilder, then run unprepared, prepared, paged and batch statements through an async API on Tokio, with derive macros for typed row (de)serialization. It handles load balancing, retry and speculative-execution policies, TLS (OpenSSL or rustls), LZ4/Snappy compression, metrics and tracing. It is not API-compatible with the DataStax cassandra.h C/C++ driver; ScyllaDB ships a separate C/C++ binding over this Rust core (scylladb/cpp-rust-driver) for that.
how_it_is_fast: On ScyllaDB the default pool keeps one connection per shard and routes each request to the shard that owns its token (shard-aware and tablet-aware routing), so the server skips cross-shard forwarding. Write coalescing, on by default, waits a small nondeterministic delay to batch several queued requests into one socket write syscall. Many requests are multiplexed per connection on a multi-threaded Tokio executor, and rows can be deserialized zero-copy from the response frame.
when_to_use: Rust services on Tokio that talk to ScyllaDB and benefit from shard-aware and tablet-aware routing.
High-concurrency write or read loads (hundreds to thousands of requests in flight), the regime the benchmark exercised with 512-8192 concurrent requests.
Rust code currently using cassandra-cpp (bindings over the DataStax C++ driver) that wants to drop the C++ library dependency without losing throughput.
Apache Cassandra clusters from Rust, where it is compatible but loses the ScyllaDB-only shard routing.
when_not_to_use: Expecting a throughput gain over the multi-threaded C/C++ driver: the only like-for-like published chart shows parity (2-7% faster at 512-4096 requests in flight, about 3% slower at 8192).

CPU-constrained clients: a later ScyllaDB write-up (search snippet only) reported the Rust driver using about twice the CPU of a cassandra-cpp backend in a loopback test, attributed to extra syscalls; write coalescing targets this, but no newer comparison was found.
Low-rate, latency-sensitive callers on a busy Tokio executor: the SessionBuilder docs warn that write coalescing may worsen latency in that case.
Programs not on Tokio, or C/C++ programs: Tokio is required, and C/C++ needs the separate cpp-rust-driver binding.

integration.dependencies: tokio 1.40+, futures; optional openssl 0.10 / tokio-openssl or rustls 0.23 / tokio-rustls for TLS; compression and other extras behind Cargo features
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.88 for crate 1.9.0 (crates.io rust_version); the main-branch README states MSRV 1.89
integration.thread_safety: not documented in the pages read; the benchmark shares one Session through Arc across 512-8192 spawned Tokio tasks

gotchas: Shard-awareness asymmetry in the harness: scylla.sh starts ScyllaDB with --smp 4, the Rust driver keeps one connection per shard and routes to the owning shard, while the DataStax cpp-driver ('cpp-multi') is not shard-aware (ScyllaDB's fork advertises shard-awareness as its addition). So part of any Rust edge here is server-side routing rather than client efficiency, and the Rust driver still only reaches parity.

The benchmark cannot be rebuilt: benchmarks/basic/scylla-rust-driver/source/Cargo.toml pins the driver to git branch main with no Cargo.lock, but main.rs imports scylla::prepared_statement, scylla::{IntoTypedRows, Session} and calls session.execute, none of which exist in today's lib.rs (Session moved to scylla::client::session, statements to scylla::statement, execute became execute_unpaged). build.sh therefore fails today, and the 2021-06-20 chart measured a pre-1.0 driver.

Chart provenance is unclear: the repo's scylla.sh describes one local 4-shard node, while the 2021 ScyllaDB blog post (snippet only) describes a 3-node Scylla 4.4 cluster on i3.4xlarge with a c5.9xlarge loader. Nothing ties the chart to either setup, and each cell is one run with no hardware or variance stated.

The headline 4.3-9.9x lead is over the Scylla C++ fork capped to one I/O thread, a limit removed from the harness on 2022-08-01 without a new chart. The 3734 vs 5510 ms figures in generate_chart/config.py are chart-generator input with no matching run.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The Tokio sibling entries (1M-task memory, TCP echo against libuv) measure the runtime this driver is built on; pick this entry only when the job is speaking CQL to ScyllaDB or Cassandra from Rust. Do not pick it for a speed edge over C++.
verified_claims_summary: Vendor chart images/bench10to7-inserts.svg (2021-06-20): 10,000,000 prepared INSERTs at 512/1024/2048/4096/8192 requests in flight, one run per cell, hardware unstated. Rust driver 12.8/9.3/7.4/6.6/6.5 s against the multi-threaded DataStax C++ driver 13.4/9.9/7.7/6.7/6.3 s (parity), and 53-64 s for the Scylla C++ fork on one I/O thread. The C++ harness was built with g++ -O3 -flto against prebuilt .deb driver packages, the Rust harness with cargo --release and lto = true.
status_note: Actively maintained and production-ready by its own statement (crate 1.9.0 released 2026-09-15, about 9.5M crates.io downloads, 689 stars, 123 open issues of which 20 are labelled performance), dual MIT/Apache-2.0. The supporting benchmark repo has been idle since 2022-08-05 and no longer builds against the driver.
